Cc: Ben Lawson <blawson@edgehealth.com>
Date: 2025-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator evidence / Order Form questions

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement asked me to capture the immediate asks so legal can align with security. We have three outstanding items before we can present to our CFO: 1) a concise list of what "operator access" looks like for on-prem deployments (console ports, temporary credentials, witness procedure), 2) the proposed escrow-like deposit for a forensic snapshot (who holds, access conditions), and 3) the redlined Order Form you mentioned with the licensing territory for on-prem nodes.

I've attached our procurement checklist (requested_evidence_matrix.xlsx) with placeholders. Could you confirm a point person for each? Our timeline is tight — execs want a clean packet by Friday EOD PST.

Appreciate it,
Maya
Maya Singh
Sr. Procurement Manager | EdgeHealth

From: ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@edgehealth.com>, Ben Lawson <blawson@edgehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator evidence / Order Form questions

Maya —

Thanks, noted. Quick answers below and a plan to deliver the artifacts: 

1) Operator access scope: David will share an operator access summary + a short runbook excerpt (we'll push an "operator-runbook-excerpt.txt" with the minimal witness steps and temporary access window policy). Temporary console access is only granted via time-limited support tokens (max 4 hours) and under a recorded remote session. No persistent creds are escrowed to us.

2) Forensic snapshot / deposit: We support a witness-based snapshot deposit model. Redwood proposes that a sealed snapshot be deposited with an independent custodian (we typically recommend a neutral third-party escrow agent) with access only on mutually-agreed triggers (court order, termination + failed remediation). Laura — legal, can you draft the minimal exhibit language and specify acceptance criteria for a deposit?

3) Order Form redlines: Attaching a redline draft (EdgeHealth_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Key notes: licensing limited to deployed nodes in the listed geo (US), derivative rights carveouts preserved, and an SLA exception for on-prem due to customer-managed infra. We'll highlight the license boundary language to make sure it aligns with the private deployment exhibit.

Action items:
- David: operator runbook excerpt + diagram (today EOD)
- Laura: draft exhibit text for snapshot deposit (tomorrow)
- Ava: consolidate packet and return updated evidence matrix to Maya by Thu EOD

I'll ping you if anything blocks.

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@edgehealth.com>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator evidence / Order Form questions

Maya — ava —

Attached is the operator excerpt and a short diagram describing operator touchpoints for a private on-prem deployment. Key constraints:
- Support tokens: issued by customer IAM with scoped role binding; Redwood requires ephemeral session tokens, recorded for audit, max 4 hour windows.
- No code or model artifacts are shipped offsite as part of day-to-day support. For witness snapshots, we can produce a cryptographic snapshot of the runtime image and associated metadata.

Also included: a checklist of the evidence we can provide immediately (SOC 2 summary, runbook extract, snapshot acceptance test plan). If EdgeHealth wants a "live" witness, we can schedule a 2-hour session with ops to validate snapshot creation; otherwise we can provide a notarized hash and deposit route.

Att: operator-runbook-excerpt.txt

David
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@edgehealth.com>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-04-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator evidence / Order Form questions

Maya / Team —

Thanks for the outline. I reviewed the proposed escrow-like language and made a few edits on scope and triggers to reduce ambiguity. Summary of legal positions: 

- Custodian: we will propose a third-party escrow (neutral) rather than Redwood holding the snapshot. Exhibit will name the custody agent class and a process to replace the agent if either party objects.
- Triggers for access: (i) court order/subpoena, (ii) insolvency/termination + failure to remediate a critical breach after cure period, (iii) mutual written consent. We do not agree to indefinite unilateral access on vague terms; the exhibit spells out a 30-day notice + remediation window for operational issues.
- Acceptance criteria: the snapshot must include a signed manifest and a notarized hash so both parties can validate integrity.
- Operator access: limiting remote access to recorded, time-limited sessions, and requiring customer IAM integration is reasonable. We added a representation that Redwood will not attempt remote persistence or create accounts without signed approval.

I'm attaching a marked exhibit (EdgeHealth_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). Please review the legal edits and call out anything you need clarified. If Procurement wants accelerated signoff, we can propose a side-letter for temporary limited witness access during onboarding.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Lawson <blawson@edgehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, ava_chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <m.singh@edgehealth.com>
Date: 2025-04-04T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator evidence / Order Form questions

Thanks — this is helpful and a lot clearer than our starting point. A couple quick follow-ups from Procurement after reviewing the edits: 

1) Custodian suggestion: can you share two recommended escrow agents you have used before (we prefer candidates with healthcare compliance experience)?
2) Snap acceptance test: Procurement would prefer a simple acceptance checklist we can use during witness to confirm snapshot integrity. Can David supply a 1-page checklist (pass/fail items) we can include in our packet?
3) Temporary access side-letter: Procurement is open to a limited side-letter for onboarding witness sessions. Can Laura propose the one-paragraph emergency access language we discussed so we can present to CFO?

If you can get these three items to us by EOD tomorrow, we should be able to keep Friday's packet deadline.

-Ben
Ben Lawson
Head of Procurement | EdgeHealth
